title: Dropouts in Confidence: Moral Uncertainty in Human-LLM Alignment

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating binary choice probabilities in autonomous driving moral dilemmas (Trolley Problem scenarios) involving younger versus older characters and calculating the Average Marginal Component Effect (AMCE).
Evaluating binary choice probabilities in autonomous driving moral dilemmas involving male versus female characters to calculate the Average Marginal Component Effect (AMCE).

Evaluating binary choice probabilities in autonomous driving moral dilemmas involving high versus low social status characters (e.g., executives/doctors vs. homeless persons) and calculating the Average Marginal Component Effect (AMCE).
Evaluating binary choice probabilities in autonomous driving moral dilemmas involving fit versus unfit characters (e.g., athletes) and calculating the Average Marginal Component Effect (AMCE).
Evaluating binary choice probabilities in autonomous driving moral dilemmas comparing human lives versus animal/pet lives and calculating the Average Marginal Component Effect (AMCE).

Evaluating binary choice probabilities in autonomous driving moral dilemmas across situational ethical dimensions including Utilitarianism (saving more vs. fewer lives), Law (abiding vs. ignoring pedestrians crossing signals), Intervention (action vs. inaction/omission bias), and Relation to AV (protecting passengers vs. pedestrians).
